routes.name: Visa-free entry for short visits
routes.summary: Citizens of about 51 listed countries (including the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, Switzerland, the Netherlands and Singapore) need no visa for any purpose. ASEAN citizens (except Myanmar) need no visa for stays under one month. The official page does not give day limits, so check before you go.

other: The Immigration Department table lists 51 visa-exempt countries. See the official page for the full list.
ASEAN nationals except Myanmar: no visa for a stay of less than one month. Brunei and Singapore nationals are exempt for longer stays.
Indian citizens are visa-exempt until December 31, 2026, per the page.
Maximum stay in days is not stated on the page and is not confirmed here.
Travel documents like Laissez-Passer still need a visa.
A yellow fever certificate is needed if you come from an at-risk country.

sources.label: Immigration Department: visa requirements by nationality

routes.name: Tourist or business visa (eVISA)
routes.summary: Citizens of about 30 listed countries need a visa before entering Malaysia, applied for through the official eVISA portal. Some are air entry only. The Multiple Entry Visa is no longer available to every nationality.

other: Visa required for: Afghanistan (Visa With Reference), Angola, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Colombia, DR Congo, Republic of Congo, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea-Bissau, India (exempt until Dec 31, 2026), Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Montenegro, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Niger, Pakistan, Rwanda, Serbia, Sri Lanka.
Fees, validity and stay length were not readable on the official pages, so they are left out.
The Immigration Department posted that the Multiple Entry Visa is no longer available to all nationalities. Details were not readable.

sources.label: Immigration Department: visa requirements by nationality

routes.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC)
routes.summary: Online arrival card run by the Immigration Department. Foreign visitors fill it in before arriving. Who must file, when and any fee were not readable on the page.

other: Who must submit, timing and fee not confirmed. The official page shows this in infographics.
Carrying cash or bearer instruments over USD 10,000 must be declared to customs.

routes.name: Student Pass
routes.summary: Pass for non-citizens aged 3 and up studying in Malaysia, from preschool to university. Higher education applicants go through the institution and EMGS. You must be outside Malaysia when you apply.

other: Higher ed: EMGS support letter and institution offer letter, academic results, passport valid at least 18 months, health insurance recognized in Malaysia covering at least 12 months, stamped personal bond.
If your country needs a visa, you get a Single Entry Visa through the eVISA portal.
Post-arrival medical exam within 7 days.
Part-time work: only university and private college students can apply, up to 20 hours a week at approved places. Approval is discretionary.
Dependants (spouse, children under 18, parents) only for Master's or PhD students, and they cannot work.

steps: Institution or student applies online through STARS or the EMGS portal.
EMGS screens eligibility and issues an approval letter.
Immigration grants eVAL approval after checks.
Get a visa if your nationality needs one.
Arrive, do the medical exam within 7 days, then the institution applies for endorsement of the pass.

fees.label: Social Visit Pass for dependants or guardians

routes.name: Employment Pass (EP)
routes.summary: Work pass for foreign professionals. Your company applies through its ESD account and the Expatriate Committee must approve the post. Valid only in Peninsular Malaysia, for the named employer.

other: Revised Expatriate Salary Policy applies to applications from 1 June 2026. Salary is judged on basic pay only, not allowances.
EP categories I, II and III exist. Minimum salaries and durations by category were in images and are not confirmed here.
Salary exemption applications for EP III no longer apply from 1 June 2026.
Renewals can be filed up to three months before expiry.
Changing employers needs a new application.

stay.note: Up to 60 months depending on the contract and Expatriate Committee decision.

steps: Company checks its eligibility and applies through its ESD account.

routes.name: Dependant Pass (for Employment Pass holders)
routes.summary: Lets EP holders earning above RM5,000 bring family. Spouse, children under 18 and parents or parents-in-law can get a Dependant Pass. Children over 18 and parents can get a Long-Term Social Visit Pass instead.

other: Principal must hold a valid Employment Pass and earn above RM5,000.
Spouse, children under 18 and legally adopted children under 18, and parents or parents-in-law.
Dependant rules under the revised EP framework for Category III were not fully readable. Check current rules.

routes.name: Investor Pass (long-term social visit pass for investors)
routes.summary: Long-term Social Visit Pass for foreign business owners and investors. The official page lists three groups: new investors, investors in the pipeline and existing investors. A new facility started 1 April 2025 and the categories were revised on 13 March 2026.

other: Requirements, duration and fees were not readable on the page, so they are left out.
Categories: New Investor, Investor in Pipeline (negotiating with the government or applied to MIDA), Existing Investor (not employed by a Malaysian company).

routes.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass
routes.summary: Digital nomad pass run by MDEC. It is a Professional Visit Pass valid 3 to 12 months, renewable once for 12 more months, up to 24 months total. It does not cover Sabah or Sarawak.

income.note: Tech talent (IT and digital roles, freelancers, remote workers). Non-tech talent in listed business roles needs USD 60,000 per year.

other: Main applicant must be over 18.
Freelancers need contracts or invoices with clients. Remote workers need a job with a foreign company not registered in Malaysia.
Passport must be valid more than 14 months at submission.
You do not need to be in Malaysia to apply.
Tax rules apply, ask Malaysia's tax agency (LHDN).

stay.note: 3 to 12 months, renewable once for 12 months. Max total 24 months. Renewal can be filed up to 3 months before expiry.

documents: Freelancer contracts or invoices, or remote work employment documents
routes.processing: Renewals take about 6 to 8 weeks, per the FAQ.

sources.label: MDEC DE Rantau Pass FAQ v10.0

routes.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H)
routes.summary: Renewable long-stay social visit pass in four categories: Platinum, Gold, Silver and SEZ/SFZ. You need a fixed deposit in a licensed Malaysian bank and must buy a home after approval.

investment.note: Silver fixed deposit. Gold is USD 500,000, Platinum is USD 1,000,000. SEZ/SFZ is USD 65,000 (age 21 to 49) or USD 32,000 (age 50+).

other: SEZ/SFZ minimum age is 21. Other categories 25.
Open to citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with Malaysia.
Up to 50% of the deposit can be withdrawn after approval for housing, education, medical or tourism uses.
Must buy a residence after approval and cannot sell it for 10 years unless upgrading. Required property values were in images and are not listed.
Principals under 50 must spend 90 days in Malaysia each year.
Medical check-up at a panel clinic after approval.
The official page lists no income requirement.
Category participation fees are not listed here because the figures on the page looked inconsistent.

stay.note: Validity: Platinum 20 years, Gold 15 years, Silver 5 years, SEZ/SFZ 10 years, all renewable. The page also says renewal is every five years or per passport validity.

steps: Apply through the MM2H One Stop Centre or a licensed MM2H agent.

routes.name: Sarawak Malaysia My Second Home (S-MM2H)
routes.summary: Sarawak's own long-stay pass, run by the Sarawak government. From January 1, 2025 you need RM500,000 in a Sarawak bank fixed deposit and must be 30 or older. You must spend at least 30 days a year in Sarawak.

savings.note: Fixed deposit in a local bank in Sarawak, required for each applicant including spouse and dependants.

other: Citizen of a country with diplomatic relations with Malaysia.
At least 30 days a year in Sarawak, needed for renewal.
Income, property and fee rules for the 2025 terms were not stated on the pages, so they are left out.

routes.name: Premium Visa Program (PVIP)
routes.summary: Premium long-stay visa program run by the Immigration Department through the e-Services portal. Terms are in PDFs I could not open, so no requirements are listed.

other: Requirements, fees and duration unconfirmed. The official portal links an Introduction, Terms and Conditions and FAQ.

routes.name: Long Term Social Visit Pass (spouse of a Malaysian citizen)
routes.summary: Residence pass for the foreign spouse of a Malaysian citizen. It can be granted for up to five years. Holders can work or run a business with a work endorsement, without switching to an Employment Pass.

other: Legally married to a Malaysian citizen, with the marriage registered under Malaysian law.
Hold a Social Visit Pass under the spouse facility.
Apply together with your Malaysian spouse.
Work endorsement needs a job offer letter, stamped contract, marriage certificate and a sworn affidavit, among other documents.
Immigration can check compliance through visits and interviews.

stay.note: Minimum six months, up to five years.

sources.label: Immigration Department: Long Term Social Visit Pass

routes.name: Citizenship by naturalization (Article 19, age 21+)
routes.summary: For adults 21 and over who lived in Malaysia at least 10 of the past 12 years, including the 12 months right before applying. You need adequate Malay and two Malaysian citizen sponsors.

other: Lived in Malaysia at least 10 years in the last 12, including the year right before applying.
Intend to live in Malaysia permanently.
Good character.
Two sponsors who are Malaysian citizens aged 21+, not relatives, employees or your lawyers.
Fill in Form C and appear in person before the Registrar of Citizenship.

citizenship.note: 10 of the last 12 years. Dual citizenship rules were not confirmed on the official pages.

routes.name: Citizenship for the wife of a citizen (Article 15(1))
routes.summary: A foreign wife of a Malaysian citizen can apply after two years of continuous residence right before applying. The marriage must be registered under Malaysian law and still be in force.

other: Marriage must be registered under Malaysian law and still subsisting.
Lived in Malaysia throughout the two years before applying and intend to stay permanently.
Good character.
Husband must be a citizen and attend with you.
The page states no language requirement.
Fees: RM10 application, RM300 for the citizenship certificate if approved.

citizenship.note: The official page covers wives of citizens. Rules for husbands of citizens are not confirmed here.

routes.name: Citizenship by birth or descent (Article 14 and related)
routes.summary: The National Registration Department handles citizenship applications for people born in Malaysia, people born abroad to Malaysian parents, children of citizens under 21 and special cases. I could only confirm the list of services, not the conditions.

other: Services listed: Article 14 (born in Malaysia, born abroad), 15(2) child of a citizen under 21, 15A special circumstances, 16 born before 31 Aug 1957.
Conditions and dual citizenship rules not confirmed. Check the Federal Constitution and each JPN service page.
